linkedin.title: We decided to stop optimizing our algorithm for time spent.
linkedin.body:
Most news apps are built to keep you scrolling as long as possible. They feed you whatever keeps your eyes glued to the screen, even if it is rage bait or sensationalism. We chose a different path.

At Headlinne, we engineered our feed to prioritize clarity and relevance instead of just engagement time. This meant making a conscious trade-off. We accept that some users might spend less time in the app because they actually get the information they need quickly.

We believe the value of news isn't in how long you stare at your phone. It is in how well informed you are when you put it down. Building technology that respects your time is a harder engineering challenge, but it is the only way to build a product that actually helps.
linkedin.cta: See how a different approach to news feels at HEADLINNE.com.

instagram.title: Global Tensions and Policy Shifts

slides.headline: Global Tensions and Policy Shifts
slides.subtitle: Five stories shaping the world today, explained in plain English.

slides.headline: Netanyahu hits back at NYC mayor
slides.explanation: Benjamin Netanyahu accused NYC Mayor Mamdani of inciting hate after the mayor threatened to arrest him over an ICC warrant. The mayor has since walked back the threat, admitting he lacks the legal authority to carry it out.

slides.headline: Oil prices dip as Iran tensions cool
slides.explanation: Oil prices dropped slightly as both the US and Iran paused their recent attacks. This provides a small moment of stability in the markets after days of uncertainty.

slides.headline: Border officer vetting under review
slides.explanation: The White House is investigating how an ICE officer involved in a deadly shooting in Maine was vetted. This review follows intense scrutiny over the officer's background and history.

slides.headline: Suspect killed after Berlin attack
slides.explanation: Police shot and killed a man suspected of driving a van into a crowd and committing a knife attack near Berlin's Pride festival. Authorities have linked the incident to an Islamist terror motive.

slides.headline: US pauses bombing campaign in Iran
slides.explanation: The US military has stopped airstrikes on Iran for a second night following advice from top officials. Leaders are now prioritizing diplomatic talks to prevent the conflict from escalating further.

instagram.caption:
From rising tensions in the Middle East to a major security investigation in Maine, here are the top five geopolitical stories you need to know today. We break down what happened and why it matters without the noise. Which of these updates surprised you the most?

instagram.title: Markets calm as tensions ease

slides.headline: Markets calm as tensions ease
slides.subtitle: Get up to speed on oil prices, the Fed, and today's biggest market moves.

slides.headline: Oil prices drop as tensions pause
slides.explanation: Oil prices fell and stock futures climbed after the U.S. and Iran paused direct attacks. This signals a brief moment of calm as Wall Street prepares for a busy week of tech earnings.

slides.headline: Treasury yields sound an inflation alarm
slides.explanation: Rising Treasury yields show that investors are nervous about whether the Federal Reserve will actually fight inflation. The market is waiting to see if the Fed backs up its words with real action.

slides.headline: Gatwick Airport water supply returns
slides.explanation: Gatwick Airport is back to normal after a water outage shut down toilets and restaurants for passengers. It was a messy day of travel for anyone moving through the airport.

slides.headline: The triple threat facing stocks
slides.explanation: Rising oil prices, higher Treasury yields, and a stronger dollar are creating a tough environment for the S&P 500. Investors are looking for safer places to park their money while the market struggles.

slides.headline: China's big chipmaker goes public
slides.explanation: CXMT is preparing for its Shanghai debut following the largest IPO in Asia. This move is a major milestone for the Chinese memory chip industry.

instagram.caption:
Markets are catching their breath today as geopolitical tensions ease slightly. From the Fed's next move to big shifts in the chip industry, here is what you need to know to start your week. Which of these stories do you think will have the biggest impact on your wallet?
